claims.text: The target material is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can calculate the melting temperature of refractory high-entropy alloys.
An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can calculate the entropy of fusion of refractory high-entropy alloys.
An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can calculate the enthalpy of fusion of refractory high-entropy alloys.
An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can calculate the volume change at the melting point of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The calculations are intended for high temperatures and pressures similar to experimental melting measurements.
The DFT free-energy approach accurately predicts melting properties by accounting for complex interactions among the alloying elements.
The accuracy of the melting-property predictions may depend on the alloy's specific composition.
The accuracy of the melting-property predictions may depend on the alloy's processing route.
The accuracy of the predictions may depend on the computational resources available.
Experimental techniques such as DSC or thermogravimetry can be used to test the predicted melting properties.
A disagreement between experimental measurements and the DFT predictions would falsify the hypothesis.
